originalTitle: Don’t drain the budget: how to save on water heating costs
summary: It’s one of the easiest ways for households to save money and cut emissions. Australian experts share tips that will have you singing efficiently in the shower
content: Australians love getting into hot water. About 15% have four or more showers a day, while nearly a third say they shower at least twice daily, a national survey by the Water Conservancy finds. Most people’s showers last five minutes or more, and one in five will spend between 10 and 15 minutes under the mist, sending up to 135 litres of water down the drain in the process. Water heating is the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in an average Australian home, and the second largest user of energy. Most hot water use happens in the shower, followed by the bath, laundry and kitchen. Water costs depend on a home’s location, use and appliances, but in some cases they can exceed $1,000 per year, particularly for households still reliant on gas hot water systems, say researchers at the University of Technology Sydney. Efficient and electric technologies can reduce those costs by 72%, or sometimes more when paired with rooftop solar. “Hot water is one of the biggest opportunities to reduce household energy costs,” says Lloyd Heathfield, the solar and electrification programs lead at Yarra Energy Foundation, noting that the shower is usually the best place to start. Simple ways to save Switching to an efficient shower head is a quick way to save on water and energy, says Tim Forcey, an independent energy consultant and the author of My Efficient Electric Home Handbook. “I’ve been in homes where there might be a shower head using 25 litres a minute, and I’ve even measured as much as 50 – it’s like standing under some sort of fire hydrant,” Forcey says. “These days you can have a nice shower with a shower head that’s using eight litres a minute,” he says, or maybe even four or less. Forcey often recommends Methven’s Kiri Satinjet as a highly efficient, pleasant-feeling shower. But there are cheaper options available, including free or subsidised showerheads under government programs, and flow restriction devices, which can be bought for a few dollars. For those willing to make behavioural changes, cutting your shower time – from 10 to four minutes – can reduce indoor water use by 25% and energy consumption by up to 15%. Modern shower timers, with traffic light alerts, can help nudge people towards shorter showers, especially for families with children, according to research by the University of Queensland. Rachael Wilkinson, a senior adviser at the Energy Efficiency Council, says other simple changes make a real difference too. “Using cold water for washing clothes, washing your hands with cold water where practical, and keeping showers a little shorter can all help reduce hot water consumption.” Beyond the shower, modern dishwashers can be more efficient on water and energy than hand washing in the sink, says Helen Oakey, the chief executive of Renew, a not-for-profit that advocates for people to live sustainably – but you should make sure it’s stacked full before running it. Heat pumps and solar panels When it comes to hot water systems, most energy experts recommend heat pumps as an efficient, electric alternative to gas or conventional electric water heating. “Hot water heat pumps are also such an easy swap to make, there’s no behaviour change needed – you turn on the tap or shower and hot water comes out – it’s just costing you much less!” Heathfield says. “A heat pump hot water system works much like a reverse-cycle air conditioner. Instead of creating heat directly, it collects heat from the surrounding air and transfers it into a tank of water.” Forcey says heat pumps do require some electricity to run the fan and compressor. “But you can heat with a hot water heat pump for a third of the cost of using gas, and even a quarter or a fifth of the cost of using electric resistive hot water systems.” The running costs get even lower when the system is powered by rooftop solar, he says, or is scheduled to switch on during a free power period on your electricity plan. For households with solar, it’s a good way to “self-consume” what you generate each day, he says. “You don’t get paid much for putting your solar electricity out on to the grid. So you might as well use it.” It does pay to plan ahead, Oakey says. People can panic when their hot water system breaks down, and end up replacing like-with-like in a rush, potentially missing out on available rebates too, she says. Homes that are only connected to gas for hot water are also paying a daily connection fee to remain on the network, and should seriously consider going electric when their unit breaks down. “Get that choice ready before it happens, because when it happens you’re probably going to be quite keen to get hot water back on in the home.” Generous federal and state rebates are available to assist with the upfront price of the product. Tools like Rewiring Australia’s Electric Saul and the Victoria government’s Easy Electric SEC can help with estimating savings and finding rebates for switching from gas to electric. A new hot water system may be a long-term investment, but Forcey agrees it’s better to weigh your options before your current unit breaks. “Chances are it’s going to fail on Christmas Eve, or it’s going to fail when you’re standing in the shower,” he says. “It’s difficult to make a sensible decision when you are cold, wet and naked.”
chineseTitle: 不要耗尽预算：如何节省热水成本
chineseSummary: 这是家庭省钱和减少排放的最简单方法之一。澳大利亚专家分享让你在淋浴时高效唱歌的技巧
chineseContent: 澳大利亚人喜欢陷入热水之中。水利部的一项全国调查发现，大约 15% 的人每天淋浴四次或更多，而近三分之一的人表示他们每天至少淋浴两次。大多数人的淋浴时间会持续五分钟或更长时间，五分之一的人会在水雾下度过 10 到 15 分钟，在此过程中多达 135 升的水被排入下水道。水加热是澳大利亚普通家庭温室气体排放的最大来源，也是第二大能源用户。大多数热水使用发生在淋浴间，其次是浴室、洗衣房和厨房。悉尼科技大学的研究人员表示，水费取决于家庭的位置、用途和电器，但在某些情况下，每年的水费可能超过 1,000 美元，特别是对于仍然依赖燃气热水系统的家庭。高效的电动技术可以将这些成本降低 72%，有时与屋顶太阳能配合使用时甚至可以降低更多。亚拉能源基金会太阳能和电气化项目负责人劳埃德·希思菲尔德 (Lloyd Heathfield) 表示：“热水是降低家庭能源成本的最大机会之一。”他指出，淋浴通常是最好的起点。简单的节水方法 独立能源顾问、《我的高效家用电器手册》一书的作者蒂姆·福西 (Tim Forcey) 表示，改用高效淋浴喷头是节水节能的快速方法。 “我曾住过一些家庭，那里的淋浴喷头每分钟的用水量为 25 升，我什至测量过多达 50 升——这就像站在某种消防栓下一样，”福西说道。 “如今，你可以用每分钟消耗八升的淋浴喷头来享受一场美妙的淋浴，”他说，甚至可能是四升或更少。 Forcey 经常推荐 Methven 的 Kiri Satinjet 作为一款高效、舒适的鞋
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
